(Abbreviated Matrix) // Homage to the Omniscient One!
Thus have I heard.

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of monks— twelve hundred and fifty monks who were all renowned elders and great disciples, each of whom was an arhat.
They were as follows: the Elder Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, Mahākapphiṇa, Mahākātyāyana, Mahākauṣṭhila, Revata, Śuddhipanthaka, Nanda, Ānanda, Rāhula, and Gavāmpati.
And with Bhāradvāja, Kālodayin, Vakkula, and Aniruddha;
with these and many other great śrāvakas,
and with a great many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Namely: Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, the Bodhisattva Ajita,
and the Bodhisattva Gandhahastin.
And by the Bodhisattva who is ever-diligent,
and by the Bodhisattva who does not cast off his burden;
and with these and many other Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas.
By Śakra, the lord of the gods, and by Brahmā, the lord of the Sahā world,
as well as by these and many other hundreds of thousands of millions of sons of gods.

Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed the venerable Śāriputra: "Śāriputra, in the western direction, beyond a hundred thousand million Buddha-fields from this world-system, there is a world-system named Sukhāvatī.
There, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Amitāyus currently resides, stays, and maintains himself."
And he teaches the Dharma. What do you think, Śāriputra, for what reason is that world-system called Sukhāvatī?
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that world-system Sukhāvatī, there is no physical suffering nor mental suffering for sentient beings;
there are only immeasurable causes of happiness.
For that reason, that world-system is called Sukhāvatī.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the world-system Sukhāvatī is adorned all around and strewn with seven railings, seven rows of palm trees,
and networks of tinkling bells made of four kinds of jewels— namely, gold, silver, beryl, and crystal— which are variegated and beautiful to behold.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, in the world-system Sukhāvatī there are lotus ponds made of the seven precious substances— namely, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, red pearl, emerald, and musāragalva as the seventh precious substance.
They were filled with water endowed with the eight qualities, with level banks, shallow enough for a crow to drink from, and strewn with golden sand.
Around those lotus ponds, in each of the four directions, were four staircases made of the four jewels—namely, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal—which were variegated and beautiful to behold.
And all around those lotus ponds, trees made of the seven jewels had grown, which were variegated and beautiful to behold.
— namely, of gold, silver, beryl, crystal, red pearl, emerald,
and the seventh jewel, musāragalva.
And in those lotus ponds there grow lotuses that are blue, blue in color, blue in luster, and blue in appearance.
Yellow ones, yellow in color, yellow in luster, and yellow in appearance;
red ones, red in color, red in luster, and red in appearance;
white ones, white in color, white in luster, and white in appearance.
Variegated, of variegated colors, with variegated lusters and variegated appearances, and as large in circumference as the wheels of a cart—
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field divine musical instruments resound perpetually;
the great earth is golden-colored and delightful.
And in that buddha-field, three times during the night and three times during the day, a rain of divine māndārava flowers falls.
There, Śāriputra, those beings who have been reborn there go to other world-systems and, with a single morning meal, pay homage to hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas.
Having showered each Tathāgata with hundreds of thousands of millions of rainfalls of flowers, they return once more to that very same world-system for their daytime rest.
Such, Śāriputra, are the arrays of qualities of that Buddha-field with which it is adorned.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field there are swans, cranes, and peacocks;
three times during the night and three times during the day they gather together and perform musical concerts, each uttering its own particular cry.
As they speak, the sound of the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment issues forth.
There, upon hearing that sound, those people give rise to mental attention directed toward the Buddha,
and mental attention directed toward the Dharma arises.
The thought of the Saṅgha arises.
What do you think, Śāriputra, are those beings born into the animal realm? You should not view it in that way.
For what reason?
Śāriputra, even the name of hells does not exist there in that buddha-field; nor is there the name of the animal realm or the world of Yama.
Furthermore, those flocks of birds were created by that Tathāgata Amitāyus and they emit the sound of the Dharma.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is thus adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field.
Furthermore, Śāriputra, in that buddha-field, when those rows of palm trees and those networks of tinkling bells are stirred by the wind,

a sweet and charming sound issues forth— just as, Śāriputra, a sweet and charming sound issues forth from a divine musical ensemble consisting of hundreds of thousands of millions of instruments played by noble beings.
In the same way, Śāriputra, when those rows of palm trees and those networks of bells are stirred by the wind, a sweet and charming sound issues forth.
When the people there hear that sound, the recollection of the Buddha becomes established in their bodies,
and the recollection of the Dharma becomes established in their bodies.
The recollection of the Saṅgha is established within the body.
Śāriputra, that buddha-field is thus adorned with such arrays of qualities of a buddha-field.
What do you think, Śāriputra, for what reason is that Tathāgata called Amitāyus?
Indeed, Śāriputra, the lifespan of that Tathāgata and of those humans is immeasurable; for that reason, he is called Amitāyus.
And, Śāriputra, ten eons have passed since that Tathāgata fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.
What do you think, Śāriputra, for what reason is that Tathāgata called Amitābha?
Furthermore, Śāriputra, the light of that Tathāgata is unimpeded throughout all buddha-fields; for that reason, he is called Amitābha.
And, Śāriputra, that Tathāgata’s community of disciples is immeasurable—those pure Arhats whose number is not easy to declare.
That Buddha-field, Śāriputra, is adorned with such arrays of qualities of a Buddha-field.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, as for those beings who have been reborn in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitāyus— pure bodhisattvas who are irreversible and bound by only one more birth— it is not easy, Śāriputra, to state the measure of those bodhisattvas, except that they are immeasurable and incalculable.
...they go [there], as stated in the *Sukhāvativyūha* (Vaidya, p.
256). Furthermore, Śāriputra, beings in that buddha-field must make a vow.
For what reason?
For indeed, Śāriputra, it is not by a mere inferior root of merit that beings are reborn in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitāyus when they encounter such noble persons.
Any son of good family or daughter of good family, Śāriputra, who hears the name of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, [will be reborn there].
Having heard it, he will attend to it;
for one night, or two nights, or three nights, or four nights, or five nights, or six nights, or seven nights, he will attend to it with an undistracted mind.
When that son of good family or daughter of good family passes away, [he will...]
As he passes away, the Tathāgata Amitāyus, surrounded by a community of disciples and honored by the virtues of bodhisattvas, will stand before him.
With an undistorted mind, he will pass away;
having passed away, he will be reborn in that very buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitāyus, in the world-system Sukhāvatī.

Therefore, Śāriputra, seeing this very purpose, I say: a son of good family or a daughter of good family should, with reverence, make a mental vow for that buddha-field—just as I, Śāriputra, am now proclaiming it.

In the same way, Śāriputra, in the eastern direction there is the Tathāgata named Akṣobhya, the Tathāgata named Merudhvaja, the Tathāgata named Mahāmeru, the Tathāgata named Meruprabhāsa, and the Tathāgata named Mañjudhvaja.

Śāriputra, headed by the Tathāgata named [Nāma], there are Buddhas, Blessed Ones, in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā; having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues,
they perform this declaration.
You should all take up this Dharma discourse called "The Acceptance by All Buddhas," which proclaims these inconceivable qualities.
In this way, Śāriputra, in the southern direction there are the Tathāgatas named Candrasūryapradīpa, Yaśaḥprabha, Mahārciḥskandha, Merupradīpa, and Anantavīrya.

With these as their leaders, Buddhas, Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges in the southern direction, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues, [utter] this declaration:
They perform [this].
You should have faith in this Dharma discourse named "The Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas. (Sukhs 12)

In this way, Śāriputra, in the western direction there is the Tathāgata named Amitāyus, the Tathāgata named Amitaskandha, the Tathāgata named Amitadhvaja, the Tathāgata named Mahāprabha, the Tathāgata named Mahāratnaketu, and the Tathāgata named Śuddharaśmiprabha.

With these as their leaders, Śāriputra, Buddhas and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the western direction, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues, [utter] this declaration:
They perform [this].
You should have faith in this Dharma discourse named "The Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas."
Likewise, in the northern direction, there is the Tathāgata named Mahārciḥskandha, the Tathāgata named Vaiśvānaranirghoṣa,
the Tathāgata named Dundubhisvaranirghoṣa, the Tathāgata named Duṣpradharṣa, the Tathāgata named Ādityasaṃbhava, the Tathāgata named Jaleniprabha, and the Tathāgata named Prabhākara.

Śāriputra, headed by these, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the northern direction, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues, perform this declaration: "Believe this Dharma discourse named 'The Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas'. (Sukhs_14)

Śāriputra, in this way, in the direction below, there are the Tathāgata named Siṃha, the Tathāgata named Yaśas, the Tathāgata named Yaśaḥprabhāsa, the Tathāgata named Dharma, the Tathāgata named Dharmadhara, and the Tathāgata named Dharmadhvaja.

With these as their leaders, Śāriputra, Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the direction below, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues, [utter] this declaration: (Note: The text fragment provided ends mid-sentence regarding the *nirveṭhana* or "declaration/explanation," which typically refers to the proclamation of the Dharma or the revelation of the Buddha’s intent.)
They perform [this].
Believe in this Dharma discourse named "The Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities and the Acceptance by All Buddhas. (Sukhs 15)
Likewise, in the direction above, there is the Tathāgata named Brahmaghoṣa, the Tathāgata named Nakṣatrarāja, the Tathāgata named Indraketudhvajarāja,
the Tathāgata named Gandhottama, the Tathāgata named Gandhaprabhāsa, the Tathāgata named Mahārciskandha,
the Tathāgata named Ratnakusumasaṃpuṣpitagātra, and the Tathāgata named Sālendrarāja.
The Tathāgata named Ratnotpalashrī, the Tathāgata named Sarvārthadarśin, and the Tathāgata named Sumerukalpa—
Śāriputra, these and other Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā in the zenith, having covered their respective Buddha-fields with their tongues,
are making this proclamation.
You should all take up this Dharma discourse named "The Acceptance by All Buddhas," which proclaims these inconceivable qualities.
What do you think, Śāriputra? For what reason is this Dharma-discourse called "The Acceptance by All Buddhas"?
Śāriputra, any sons of good family or daughters of good family who hear the name of this Dharma-discourse shall hold the names of those Blessed Buddhas in their minds.
All of them will be sustained by the Buddhas and will become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Therefore, Śāriputra, you should have faith, believe, and do not doubt me or those Blessed Buddhas.

Śāriputra, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family shall make a mental vow for the buddha-field of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amitāyus— whether they have already made it, are making it, or will make it— all of them shall become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
They will be reborn in that buddha-field,
or have been reborn, or are being reborn there.
Therefore, Śāriputra, faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family should generate the aspiration for that buddha-field.
Just as, Śāriputra, I now proclaim these inconceivable qualities of those Buddhas,
the Blessed Ones, even so, Śāriputra, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, also proclaim these inconceivable qualities of me.
A most difficult task has been performed by the Blessed One, Śākyamuni, the sovereign king of the Śākyas.

Having awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this Sahā world-system, he taught a Dharma that is contrary to the expectations of the entire world, amidst the degeneration of the eon, the degeneration of sentient beings, the degeneration of views, the degeneration of lifespan,
and the degeneration of afflictions.
Therefore, Śāriputra, it is also extremely difficult for me that, having awakened to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment in the Sahā world-system,

I have taught a Dharma that is contrary to the expectations of all the world, amidst the corruption of beings, the corruption of views, the corruption of afflictions, the corruption of lifespan, and the corruption of the eon.
The Blessed One having spoken this, the Venerable Śāriputra, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "The Array of Sukhāvatī"
